history.summary: The generic CSV name 'Shiv Mandir' is AMBIGUOUS in Dibrugarh, which has several documented Shiva temples (e.g. Shiv Mandir on T R Phukan Road, Chowkidinghee; a small temple on Assam Trunk Road opposite Dibrugarh University; Shiv Mandir at Basanta Nagar). This entry documents the best-documented referent, the Aaprupi Shiv Mandir near Dibrugarh railway station. Per MyAdhyatm, it was established in 1818 under the inspiration of Shridevi Sharan Pandey with the help of Marwari devotees: while bathing in the river, Pandey's foot struck a stone that turned out to be a shivalinga, which he placed under a peepal tree; worship grew from there, the shrine was enlarged over time, and the temple was renovated by its committee in 2000. These details rest on a single online source and should be corroborated. Coordinates are approximate (near the town railway station).

name: Aaprupi Shiv Mandir
town_description: Dibrugarh is Upper Assam's largest city, known as the 'Tea City of India', set on the south bank of the Brahmaputra. It is a commercial hub of the tea, oil and gas industries and home to Dibrugarh University and the Assam Medical College.

travel.airport: Dibrugarh Airport (Mohanbari, DBR), about 15 km from the city centre
travel.railway: Dibrugarh Town railway station is nearby
travel.road: NH-15 and NH-515 connect Dibrugarh to Tinsukia, Jorhat and Guwahati

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the weather is cool and dry
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented; Maha Shivaratri is the main annual festival, verify timings locally
